sentences.text: 3. Heard the arguments of Sri. Arun Sham, learned Senior counsel for Sri. Suyog Herele E., learned counsel for the petitioners in both the petitions and Smt. N. Anitha Girish, learned High Court Government Pleader for State.
It is the contention of the learned Senior counsel for the petitioner that the victim is working as a junior Engineer in Jilla Panchayath, Mangaluru.
She came in contact with accused No.1 and they fell in love and thereafter, due to differences, they have parted away.
For the reason of the same, the victim has filed a complaint NC: 2023:KHC:37725 through her sister.
The allegations made in the complaint clearly points out that accused No.1 and the victim, due to love, they came in contact physically.
The victim is an Engineer and not an illiterate and anything happened between the accused No.1 and the victim was due to consensus.
Utmost the allegation of refusing to marry may attract the offence punishable under Section 417 of IPC, which is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
The petitioner/accused No.1 is ready to abide by any conditions.

In Crl.P. No.10649/2023:
The petitioner/accused No.2 is concerned, he has assisted the accused No.1 in the love affair with the victim.
His name is not mentioned in the FIR as accused but he is apprehending arrest.
He is nothing to do with the love affair, physical contact as well as promise of marriage.
He is ready to abide by the conditions.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has contended that the petitioner/accused No.1 has promised the victim that he will marry her and both fell in love.
Misusing the NC: 2023:KHC:37725 situation, he had physical contact with the victim and now without any reason, he is giving lame excuses for not marrying the victim.
The other petitioner/accused No.2 has assisted accused No.1 in these activities.
Hence, there is a prima facie case against both.
If bail is granted, they will tamper the evidence.
6. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and perused the records.
7. The allegations did point out that the victim is major, an engineering graduate, working as a junior Engineer in Jilla Panchayath, Engineering Division, Mangaluru.
While working, she came in contact with the accused No.1.

Both fell in love, proceeded further and they came in physical contact thereafter, differences arose between the accused No.1 and the victim and he refused to marry her and for this reason, the victim made attempts to commit suicide by consuming poison.
8.

There is an allegation that the petitioner in Crl.P. No.10649/2023, being a friend of accused No.1,
has NC: 2023:KHC:37725 assisted his friend in refusing to marry the victim.

The allegations did clearly point out that by mutual consent both the victim and the accused No.1 were in physical relationship and the proposal of the victim to marry has been refused by the accused No.1 resulting some untoward incident and therefore, law is set into motion against accused No.1.

sentences.text: In total consideration of the materials on record, there is no prima facie material which attracts the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC.
Utmost the offence under Section 417 of IPC for breach of promise of marriage may attract, which is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
Accused No.1 has already been arrested, interrogated and is no more required for investigation.
10. The petitioner in Crl.P. No.10649/2023 is only a person, who assisted the accused No.1.
I do not found any material which attracts any of the offences alleged against accused No.1.
Both the petitioners undertaken to NC: 2023:KHC:37725 abide by any conditions that would be imposed against them.
11. In the facts and circumstances of the case, I do not found any reason to refuse exercise of discretion in grant of bail.
Conditions will meet the apprehension of the prosecution.
Hence, both petitions deserve merit consideration.

In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) Both the Petitions are allowed.

(ii) The petitioner/accused No.2 is ordered to be released on bail in the event of his arrest and the petitioner/accused No.1 is ordered to be released on bail in Crime No.82/2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 417 and 376 of IPC, on each of them executing personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one like bond to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer.
